title.narrative: Enhanced constituents' capacity to ensure compliance with fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative:
Over the past few years, Egypt has achieved significant progress in strengthening its response to child labour through institutional, legal, and policy reforms, developed with technical support from the International Labour Organization (ILO) Cairo Office. Despite these advancements, child labour remains a critical challenge, particularly in rural areas and informal sectors such as agriculture, small-scale manufacturing, and the lower tiers of supply chains.
In collaboration with tripartite constituents, nine National Steering Committee (NSC) meetings were held to monitor progress and address challenges in implementing the *National Action Plan for Combating the Worst Forms of Child Labour and Supporting Families in Egypt*, which concluded in 2025. Through the NSC, national and sectoral tools were developed to enhance prevention, identification, referral, and remediation mechanisms, effectively supporting the operationalization of the Child Labour Monitoring System. Following the conclusion of this plan, a second-generation National Action Plan is slated for development in 2026, expanding its focus to encompass child labour, forced labour, discrimination, and occupational safety and health (OSH).
These developments reflect Egypt’s growing commitment to achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 8.7 and advancing the objectives of Egypt Vision 2030. Furthermore, to drive evidence-based policymaking, a new edition of the National Child Labour Survey has been produced. This survey generates updated data on hazardous work and trafficking-related child labour and is currently awaiting its official launch.
Following the adoption of a new Labour Code in 2025, upcoming priorities center on institutional capacity-building for the Ministry of Labour’s Labour and OSH Inspection Department. Further support is required to revise inspection checklists to properly integrate the updated provisions of the Labour Code and Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW).
